messages.author: 412aa207a5583264
messages.subject: Parser warning from example Multivariate Probit
parts:
Hi all,
     I'm working on a multivariate probit model. But, I'm confused because the example code from the manual produces the following warning: 

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    z ~ multi_normal_cholesky(...)

What I'm trying to compile is identical to the code that lives at https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/misc/multivariate-probit/probit-multi.stan, excluding a replacement of the '<-' assignments to '='. A couple of questions about this warning:

1) Can I safely ignore it? 

2) If it is a false positive, what set it off? 

Thanks so for your time,
Patrick

messages.author: 412aa207a5583264
messages.subject: Re: Parser warning from example Multivariate Probit
parts:
Hi Ben,
     Thanks for the quick reply. As you may have guessed that I'm pretty new to this, and I'm not sure how to provide the most useful information.

On Saturday, September 17, 2016 at 2:10:19 PM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Saturday, September 17, 2016 at 1:58:54 PM UTC-4, Patrick Sadil wrote:
1) Can I safely ignore it? 

http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#parser-warnings

Does the function that fills z have a constant derivative?

I'm sorry, but I'm not entirely sure. I think so? By 'function that fills z' do you mean the line: z ~ multi_normal_cholesky(beta_x, L_Omega); ? If so, then I'd assume so since there's nothing nonlinear about beta_x (which is just the result of a multiplication of a coefficient matrix with the design matrix). But, do you instead mean the part in the transformed parameters block: 

transformed parameters {
  vector[D] z[N];
  for (n in 1:N_pos)
    z[n_pos[n], d_pos[n]] = z_pos[n];
  for (n in 1:N_neg)
    z[n_neg[n], d_neg[n]] = z_neg[n];
}
 
where the latent variable, z, is being constructed from z_pos and z_neg (which were themselves given implicit, improper uniform priors)?

2) If it is a false positive, what set it off? 

Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    z ~ multi_normal_cholesky(...)

To clarify, what I'm confused about is why the parser would have told me that there might be a non-linear transform on the left-hand side of this sampling statement when there's nothing besides the 'z' to the left of the '~'.
 
Thanks again,
Patrick

Yes

To clarify, what I'm confused about is why the parser would have told me that there might be a non-linear transform on the left-hand side of this sampling statement when there's nothing besides the 'z' to the left of the '~'.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Parser warning from example Multivariate Probit
parts:
On Saturday, September 17, 2016 at 5:21:34 PM UTC-4, Patrick Sadil wrote:
Okay. So, is it accurate to summarise this as, the parser threw a warning at the sampling statement because it was being asked to perform operations on the target for a variable that was not declared in the parameters block?
Yes, although not just any operation but rather one that increments the posterior kernel in log units.

Could I safely avoid the warning by instead transforming my data outside of stan? So, rather passing an N by D array, y, of 0s and 1s, I would instead give stan an N by D matrix of reals such that each 0 is replaced by a call to

> runif(n=1, min = -1, max = 0)

and each 1 is replaced by  

> runif(n = 1, min = 0, max = 1)?

Then, the sampling statement could just be:

    y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(beta_x, L_Omega);

That would avoid the parser warning and have the side effect of estimating a completely different model that is neither a multivariate probit model nor a model where y depends on x.

It would be better to estimate the multivariate probit model and either increment the target keyword by the logarithm of the absolute value of the derivative of the transformation from z to its parent variable(s) or recognize that this derivative is a constant (indeed 1.0), in which case you would be incrementing the target keyword by a constant (indeed 0.0) which has no effect on what values are proposed for the parameters of what proposals are accepted. Better still would be to understand the principles behind a change-of-variables including the circumstances when essentially nothing is changed.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Parser warning from example Multivariate Probit
parts:
First, y ~ foo(theta) statements don't fill in y. y has
to be defined before they're called and it just increments
the log desnity.

Second, you can't move parameter transforms into the preprocessor
because they depend on parameters at every step. The transformed
parameters block is this:

transformed parameters {
vector[D] z[N];
for (n in 1:N_pos)
z[n_pos[n], d_pos[n]] <- z_pos[n];
for (n in 1:N_neg)

z[n_neg[n], d_neg[n]] <- z_neg[n];
}

And it's just defining all of z in terms of z_pos and z_neg.
So there's nothing non-linear there, so the

The sampling statement in question is just

z ~ multi_normal_cholesky(beta_x, L_Omega);

So that's OK.

- Bob
